prerequisites: Knowledge of Physics (units, magnitudes, physical principles)
Knowledge of Mathematics (algebra, trigonometry, and differential calculus)
Knowledge of Graphic Expression (spatial vision, interpretation of diagrams)
Having completed the Mechanics course in the third semester (kinematics and dynamics of rigid bodies)

learning_outcomes.text: Develop digital skills for the dynamic analysis of industrial cases.
Recognize the mechanisms present in a machine and be able to model it.
Solve kinematics and dynamics of mechanisms and machines using Newtonian and energetic methods.
Know methods for synthesis and kinematic analysis of articulated, cam, or gear mechanisms.
Understand dynamic problems of machinery such as balancing or cyclic operation.
Knows the various machine elements and understands their operation.

syllabus_topics: Mechanisms: nomenclature, typologies, mobility. Introduction to mechanism synthesis.
Kinematic analysis of articulated mechanisms. Position, velocity, and acceleration problems.
Analysis and design of mechanisms of special interest: cams and gear trains.
Dynamic analysis methods in machines: vectorial dynamics, energy, virtual powers theorem.
Balancing. Application to rotors and mechanisms.
Study of the cyclic operation of machines.
teaching_methods: Study, learning, and resolution of proposed numerical examples
assessment_rules: To pass, a minimum grade of 5.0 must be obtained in both the practices part and the knowledge test. In official calls, if the practices part has already been passed, only the knowledge test needs to be taken. The use of non-permitted materials or electronic devices during an evaluation test may result in a failing grade of 0.
